sections.title: Executive investment summary: a regulator-anchored testing utility priced as a compounder

blocks.text: Vimta Labs Limited is a Hyderabad-headquartered contract research and testing organisation (CRTO). It sells laboratory hours and scientific judgement, not products: customers send samples, molecules, devices or study protocols, and Vimta returns data and reports that go into regulatory dossiers, product releases and import/export clearances. [F] (AR2026 p.9) The company describes its offering under two service segments - Contract Research and Testing (pharma preclinical, clinical, cGMP analytical; plus food, environment and electronics testing) and, from FY27, Contract Research and Development services for Biologics and peptides. [MC] (CALL Jul 2026)

Revenue is recognised entirely as "Sale of services - Testing and Analysis", Rs 407.3 crore in FY26 against Rs 344.0 crore in FY25. [F] (AR2026 p.146) There is **no reported segment split in the audited accounts**: the Managing Director, as Chief Operating Decision Maker, reviews the company as a single operating segment, so no segment revenue or segment margin is disclosed anywhere in the annual report. [F] (AR2026 p.162)

[E] Within exports, management says roughly 60% is the United States, i.e. of the order of one-fifth to one-quarter of total revenue. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jul 2026)

Customer profile: pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical sponsors (generic filers, 505(b)(2)/NDA work and product release), food manufacturers, processors, exporters and regulators (FSSAI, BIS, APEDA, EIC), agrochemical and specialty chemical companies, medical device makers, and defence/electronics OEMs. [F] (AR2026 p.9) Management claims 90% of India's top 20 pharma companies and 7 of India's top 10 food companies as customers. [MC] (PPT Jul 2026) **No customer is named anywhere in the annual report, the presentation or any transcript, and no top-5 or top-10 concentration figure is disclosed.** [F] (AR2026 p.152)

Listing status: Vimta is not a recent listing. It has been listed on BSE and NSE since an IPO around 1991 (the APIDC Investment Agreement of 27 June 1991 was entered into "at the time of the Initial Public Offer") and filed its 36th Annual Report for FY26. [F] (AR2026 p.77) (AR2026 p.12) The evidence base is therefore a mature one - 36 years of statutory accounts, four quarterly calls and a credit rating - but it is unusually thin on operating disclosure: no segments, no order book, no customer concentration, no utilisation percentages.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: **1. Every fair value in our DCF sits far below the traded price.** Bear Rs 49.9, base Rs 79.6, bull Rs 103.6 per share against a price of Rs 630, i.e. -92.1%, -87.4% and -83.6%. The model's own reverse-DCF says today's enterprise value requires about 102.4% annual sales growth for five years against a 9.6% base-case equivalent. [F] (NUMBERS) Even after allowing for the model's stale revenue base (below), nothing in the documents supports a growth rate remotely near that. [AI]

**2. The Rs 500 crore revenue goal has been missed and rolled twice, and the run-rate goal was abandoned mid-year.** The goal was originally set "almost 5, 6 years ago" for FY26 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); in Nov 2025 management was "still sticking to that goal" of a Rs 500 cr exit run-rate [MC] (CALL Nov 2025); in Jan 2026 the Rs 125 cr quarterly run-rate was conceded - "Maybe not, we may not touch that number" [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); FY26 closed at Rs 416.3 cr total income [F] (AR2026 p.12); by May 2026 the target had become FY27 [MC] (CALL May 2026); by Jul 2026 management would only say "we are on track with respect to our growth momentum" [MC] (CALL Jul 2026).

**3. The largest single shareholder is a named competitor, and is also a related-party supplier.** Eurofins Analytical Services India Pvt Ltd holds 88,07,336 shares, 19.72% of equity - larger than the founder's 11.63%. [F] (AR2026 p.138) Eurofins is named by Vimta's own executives as a competitor in food and pharma. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) In FY26 Vimta received services worth Rs 56.88 million from Eurofins DiscoverX Products, LLC (up from Rs 27.61 mn), with Rs 9.74 mn payable at year end. [F] (AR2026 p.157) The annual report nowhere discusses the strategic implications of this holding. [F]

**4. Disclosure is materially below what the business would allow.** No segment reporting [F] (AR2026 p.162); no segment margins ("that information is not available") [MC] (CALL May 2026); no order book or backlog anywhere; no top-5/top-10 customer concentration ("it's not really relevant") [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); no capacity utilisation percentage ("we wouldn't really define capacities as percentages") [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); no capex split by vertical ("that's very granular information") [MC] (CALL Nov 2025); no remaining-performance-obligation disclosure under Ind AS 115 despite revenue recognition being the sole Key Audit Matter. [F] (AR2026 p.111)

**5. Capital intensity is rising faster than revenue.** Capex Rs 45.0 cr, Rs 49.2 cr, Rs 76.3 cr, Rs 79.1 cr, Rs 99.8 cr FY22-FY26 [F] (PPT Jul 2026) against revenue up from Rs 279.7 cr to Rs 416.3 cr. CARE puts fixed-asset turnover at 0.88x as at 31 Mar 2026 and notes the gross asset base rose 89% between FY21 and FY26. [F] (RATING) FY26 capex of Rs 99.7 cr exceeded PAT of Rs 77.5 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.116) (AR2026 p.115)

**6. FY26 operating cash flow is flattered by items that are not operating.** Cash generated from operations of Rs 170.8 cr includes a Rs 21.3 cr increase in "other current liabilities" [F] (AR2026 p.116); the balance sheet shows other non-current liabilities rose Rs 18.4 cr, of which Rs 14.5 cr is an "Advance received for purchase of Property, Plant & Equipment" (nil in FY25) and Rs 3.8 cr is EPCG deferred grant income. [F] (AR2026 p.150) On our read roughly Rs 19 cr of the Rs 147.1 cr reported operating cash flow is capital or grant related rather than trading cash. [E]

**7. Receivable quality deteriorated even as the provision was released.** Bad debts written off jumped to Rs 7.30 cr in FY26 from Rs 1.77 cr, and were charged directly to the P&L rather than against the allowance (write-offs against provisions were nil in FY26 vs Rs 2.42 cr in FY25). [F] (AR2026 p.147) (AR2026 p.142) At the same time the impairment allowance was cut from Rs 8.10 cr to Rs 6.10 cr and a net Rs 0.49 cr was written back. [F] (AR2026 p.142) Receivables over one year old but still classified "considered good" rose to Rs 6.30 cr from Rs 3.65 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.142)

**8. Promoter holding is low, falling every quarter, and the board is a family board.** Promoters 35.66% at Jun 2026, down 1.01 percentage points in a year and down every single quarter from 37.00% at Sep 2023. [F] (NUMBERS) Four of eight directors are executives, of whom three are promoter family or spouses; the Company Secretary is the spouse of an Executive Director and the Managing Director is the Chairman's daughter. [F] (AR2026 p.64) Three relatives of KMP are on the payroll. [F] (AR2026 p.156)

**9. Executive pay rose an order of magnitude faster than employee pay.** Managing Director and Executive Director remuneration rose 36.64% and ED-Operations 34.37% in FY26, against a 4% rise in median employee remuneration and 8.56% average. [F] (AR2026 p.46) Directors' remuneration was Rs 9.20 cr, 11.9% of PAT. [F] (AR2026 p.146) [E] The 78-year-old Executive Chairman is proposed for a further five-year term at Rs 18 lakh a month plus up to 1% of net profits. [F] (AR2026 p.180)

**10. Concentration of physical operations.** Both central laboratories, the Life Sciences campus, the E&E laboratory and the registered office are in Hyderabad; the food branch network is six small labs plus the FSSAI-owned NFL at Navi Mumbai and one Kolkata liaison office. [F] (AR2026 p.23) (AR2026 p.75) A quality or regulatory event at Cherlapally or Genome Valley would hit the large majority of revenue. The annual report identifies quality-audit failure as its first-named risk. [F] (AR2026 p.23)

**11. Export revenue is unhedged.** The company states plainly that it "does not undertake any hedging activities". [F] (AR2026 p.76) With Rs 152.8 cr of FY26 foreign revenue and only Rs 30.7 cr of foreign-exchange outgo [F] (AR2026 p.55), the net exposure is large; a 5% USD move is disclosed as Rs 1.45 cr of profit impact on balance-sheet monetary items alone, and management has already attributed part of the Q1 FY27 margin decline to rupee appreciation. [F] (AR2026 p.151) [MC] (CALL Jul 2026)

**12. Growth has been lumpy, not linear, and Q1 FY27 was flat sequentially.** Total income by quarter: Rs 99.3 cr, Rs 104.5 cr, Rs 100.5 cr, Rs 112.0 cr, Rs 112.9 cr (Q1 FY26 to Q1 FY27). [F] (PPT Jul 2026) (CALL Nov 2025) (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL May 2026) Q3 FY26 fell quarter-on-quarter on "unexpected operational challenges in the analytical services" and "lag in booking clinical research orders"; the quantum of deferred revenue was refused - "that is too nitty-gritty". [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

blocks.caption: Debates that decide the outcome
rows: Is the 36% EBITDA margin structural or a capacity-cycle artefact?

Four consecutive years of expansion through wage and reagent inflation, plus the exit from low-margin diagnostics, points to mix and pricing. Management: margins are "among the best in the industry even by global standards" [MC] (CALL May 2026)

The step-up coincides with the diagnostics divestment (FY25 restatement) and with a capex cycle whose depreciation is only now landing: depreciation rose from Rs 35.3 cr to Rs 43.8 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.115). Whether FY27 EBITDA margin holds above 35% while the new 200,000 sq ft fills and depreciation steps up again
Do the DCF outputs mean anything?
They are internally consistent and the reverse DCF is a legitimate reality check on an 8.6x EV/sales, 25.1x EV/EBITDA multiple [F] (NUMBERS)

The model's base revenue is a trailing twelve months of Rs 329 cr ending Dec 2024 [F] (NUMBERS), about 21% below the Rs 416.3 cr the company actually reported for FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.12) [E]. A 15% WACC and a capex rule tied to fixed-asset turnover also suppress free cash flow. Fair values are therefore biased low and the 102.4% implied growth is partly an artefact

Any disclosure of intent, a creeping-acquisition filing, or an open offer
Is the Rs 500 crore number guidance?
Management repeatedly reaffirmed it when asked and calls it "a stretch number, but definitely doable" at 20-25% growth [MC] (CALL May 2026)

Management simultaneously insists "Vimta does not give any forward projections on its numbers" [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). It is an aspiration that investors have been treating as a commitment, and it has already slipped a year
FY27 revenue against Rs 500 cr; and whether management repeats the number in the Nov 2026 call
Does biologics CRADS deserve any value today?
Rs 35 cr budget, labs commissioned, first order booked, and it plugs a gap in an existing client base of 90% of India's top-20 pharma [MC] (PPT Jul 2026) (CALL Jul 2026)

One order, domestic, size undisclosed, customer undisclosed, duration undisclosed; management expects significance only "from the third year onwards" [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); CARE expects "meaningful revenue generation by FY27-end" [F] (RATING)
A disclosed biologics revenue line, or a second and third order with stated scale

blocks.text: The consensus framing of Vimta is a high-quality Indian CRO compounder with a widening moat. Our variant reading is narrower and more specific: **Vimta is best understood as a regulated testing utility with two genuinely protected franchises - the FSSAI-conferred food positions and the accredited GLP/GCP/cGMP pharma stack - wrapped in a family holding company that discloses the minimum the law requires.** The protected franchises are real and were independently conferred, not self-claimed [F] (AR2026 p.9) (RATING). But the disclosure regime means an outside investor cannot verify concentration, cannot see a backlog, cannot see segment economics, and cannot separate the margin contribution of the moated work from the commoditised work that management itself concedes exists ("for some services which are very routine, low technology, low science, those kind of services price competition will always be there") [MC] (CALL May 2026). Meanwhile the register tells a story the narrative does not: the single largest holder is a global competitor, the second largest non-promoter holder is an instrument distributor, promoter holding is under 36% and falling, and management pay is compounding at four to nine times the pace of employee pay. The debate that actually matters is not whether the moat exists - it does - but whether a minority shareholder buying at 8.6x sales and 25.1x EV/EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS) is being paid to accept that information and control asymmetry. [AI]

blocks.text: Disclosure gap: the Q4 FY26 earnings call of 6 May 2026 discusses a US subsidiary "that has been approved". The FY26 Annual Report, signed the same day, states that "the Company did not have any subsidiary" during the year, that no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, and that no material changes occurred after year end. [F] (AR2026 p.76) (AR2026 p.27) (AR2026 p.33) The US entity is not mentioned anywhere in the annual report. The two disclosures are not reconciled. [AI]

Consequences for the analysis: because there is no subsidiary, there are no consolidated accounts. CARE's analytical approach is standalone and its list of entities consolidated is "Not applicable". [F] (RATING) Our statements data is labelled consolidated but, for FY25 and FY26, consolidated and standalone are the same entity. [AI] This matters directly: the earlier research notes on this dashboard warn that "on a consolidated basis it is materially worse than the standalone numbers... ROCE 17.6%, ROE 13.5%, P/E 45.7" [F] (BOARD). On the evidence in the accounts that gap is not a consolidation effect at all - it is a vintage effect. Those ratios correspond to the FY24 year in our statements data (RoE 13.7%, RoCE 18.0%) [F] (NUMBERS), whereas the audited FY26 figures are RoE 16.97% and RoCE 21.18%. [F] (AR2026 p.163) The board note's framing should not be relied on. [AI]

Twelve companies are listed in which directors or their relatives are interested - Bloomedha Info Solutions, Covide Business Integrated, three Escientia entities, Avanti Frozen Foods, SPANV Medisearch Lifesciences, Avanti Pet Care, Saveera Institute of Medical Sciences, Avanti Feeds, Avantel and Sarvejana Healthcare. [F] (AR2026 p.156) None is a subsidiary, associate or joint venture; transactions with them are small (see the related-party analysis in the operations part). No non-compete or common-pursuit disclosure appears anywhere in the annual report. [F]

items: **The company is old but the current shape of it is three years old.** Roughly half of today's gross block was added after FY23: gross PPE rose from Rs 315.1 cr at 1 Apr 2024 to Rs 527.3 cr at 31 Mar 2026, a 67% increase in two years. [F] (AR2026 p.137) (AR2026 p.138) [E] Genome Valley, the second EMI/EMC chamber, and the biologics suite are all FY25-FY26 assets. The revenue that is supposed to fill them does not yet exist. [AI]

**The margin history has a discontinuity in it.** FY24 total income of Rs 292.3 cr in the annual report's own five-year chart is lower than FY23's Rs 321.6 cr [F] (AR2026 p.4), because FY24 and FY25 are restated for continuing operations excluding diagnostics [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Our statements data, which is not restated, shows FY23 and FY24 sales both at Rs 318 cr. [F] (NUMBERS) Any four-year margin CAGR therefore compares a post-divestment business with a pre-divestment one. [AI]

**The regulator relationship is genuinely long-dated but finite.** The FSSAI NFL concession runs 25 years from 2021 and ends with all installed assets transferring to FSSAI for no consideration. [F] (AR2026 p.164) That is a depreciating right, accounted for as an intangible "operating right" with a net carrying value of Rs 4.93 cr at 31 Mar 2026, down from Rs 6.42 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.137) Renewal terms are not disclosed. [F]

**Ownership has drifted away from the founders for at least three years.** Promoter holding fell in ten of the eleven quarters from Sep 2023 (37.00%) to Jun 2026 (35.66%). [F] (NUMBERS) The bonus issue doubled the share count without changing economics; the ESOP plan, priced at face value, transfers value to employees at a rate of Rs 4.99 cr of expense in FY26 alone. [F] (AR2026 p.139) (AR2026 p.146)

**The listed history contains an unresolved legal thread.** The 1991 APIDC Investment Agreement "remains sub judice", disclosed twice in the annual report with no description of the claim, the amount, or the forum. [F] (AR2026 p.33) (AR2026 p.77) That is a 35-year-old open item on the company's own capital structure. [AI]

sections.title: How the service chain works and where the value is captured

items: **Step 1 - Accreditation and approval (the entry ticket).** Vimta maintains NABL ISO/IEC 17025, NABCB ISO 17065, BIS, TEC, OECD-GLP, CCSEA, DSIR, AAALAC, FSSAI, APEDA, EIC, EU Commission and Tea/Spices Board scopes, and is inspected by USFDA, EMA, WHO, NGCMA and DCGI. [F] (RATING) (PPT Jul 2026) This is a continuous cost, not a one-off: the company reports scope expansion under NABL as an ongoing revenue driver in food. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) A WHO audit of the clinical research division was completed in Q2 FY26. [MC] (CALL Nov 2025)

[F] (AR2026 p.17) (AR2026 p.151) [E] Management independently put the 2030 figure at "approximately USD300 million". [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**Illustrative share arithmetic, labelled and not a forecast [E]:** if Vimta held 5% of that USD 780 mn Indian analytical testing outsourcing pool in 2035, it would earn roughly Rs 369 crore from that single sub-market - about 91% of the company's entire FY26 revenue, ten years out. If it held 10%, roughly Rs 738 crore. These are arithmetic illustrations of how TAM translates at plausible shares; they are not projections, they use a spot exchange rate held constant, and **no part of any valuation in this report uses them.** [E]

**The conversion problem in one line:** Vimta's FY26 revenue of Rs 407 crore is about USD 43 million at the disclosed year-end rate. [E] Against a global CRO TAM of USD 91.4 billion, that is 0.05%. Quoting the global TAM alongside the company's growth rate creates an impression of runway that the delivery economics of testing do not support. [AI]

blocks.text: The defensible way to size Vimta's opportunity from these documents is bottom-up, from capacity and capability rather than from market size. [AI] Three levers exist and all three are disclosed: (i) **fill the space** - approximately 80,000 of the new 200,000 sq ft is unoccupied on management's estimate, which on a blended revenue-per-square-foot basis is worth of the order of Rs 54 crore of annual revenue, subject to the heavy caveats set out in the capacity section [E] [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); (ii) **raise the export share** - foreign revenue is 37.5% and management is investing in overseas business development, with Q1 FY27 at about 40% [F] (AR2026 p.146) [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); (iii) **add the new vertical** - biologics CRADS, which management expects to be meaningful from year three. [MC] (CALL Jul 2026)

Against those, three bottom-up constraints: fixed-asset turnover of 0.88x means new revenue requires new capital at roughly 1.7 rupees per rupee of annual revenue on the recent cycle [F] (RATING) [E]; the electronics vertical cannot scale without new laboratories in new states, which management has deferred for FY27 [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); and the food vertical has roughly half its revenue tied to trade flows that are currently disrupted [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). A bottom-up frame produces a business that can plausibly compound in the low-to-mid teens with continuing capital intensity - not one that scales into a USD 91 billion TAM. [AI]

Large multinational CROs are expanding portfolios through acquisitions in advanced modalities, bioanalysis, toxicology, and digital clinical platforms." [F] (AR2026 p.21)

blocks.text: **Two structural features of the model must be stated before any output is quoted.** First, **the base period is the twelve months to December 2024.** [F] (NUMBERS) Since then the company has reported audited FY26 total income of Rs 416.3 crore and revenue from operations of Rs 407.3 crore. [F] (AR2026 p.12) (AR2026 p.115) The model's base of Rs 329 crore is therefore about 21% below the company's most recent full-year revenue. [E] Second, **the enterprise value used for the reverse DCF does not net off cash**: the model states explicitly that "Screener's public page does not split cash out of other assets, so cash is not netted off", and shows investments as zero, while the audited balance sheet carries Rs 72.1 crore of cash, deposits and mutual funds. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.114) Both features push fair values down and implied growth up. We flag them; we do not adjust for them, because the task permits no new valuation figures. [AI]

**Model Year 1 has already been overtaken by reality.** The base case projects Year-1 sales of Rs 358.9 crore. Vimta reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 407.3 crore and total income of Rs 416.3 crore - between 13% and 16% above the model's Year 1 - and Q1 FY27 total income of Rs 112.9 crore. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.115) (PPT Jul 2026) [E] Read literally, the company is already running roughly a year and a half ahead of the base-case revenue path, which is what the stale base period would predict. The base-case **growth rates** of 9.1% to 10.0% are nonetheless below the 19.5% the company delivered in FY26 and below the 13.7% year-on-year it delivered in Q1 FY27. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] Notably, CARE reports Vimta's actual fixed-asset turnover at 0.88x, which would be far more punitive, while management claims 1.0-1.2x. [F] (RATING) [MC] (CALL Jul 2026)

sections.title: Final thesis

items: **A regulator has delegated statutory laboratory infrastructure to this company for twenty-five years, and a second regulator has notified one of its labs as a national reference laboratory.** These are facts conferred by third parties, not marketing claims, and no competitor can purchase them. **The financial record is genuinely good.** Total income from Rs 279.7 crore to Rs 416.3 crore over FY22-FY26 with the EBITDA margin rising from 29% to 36% and PAT margin from 15% to 19%, while exports more than doubled from Rs 70.7 crore to Rs 152.8 crore. **The balance sheet is close to pristine and the accounting is clean.** Net cash, 124x interest cover, undrawn bank lines, Rs 1.95 crore of contingent liabilities, no pledge, no guarantee, no off-balance-sheet vehicle, an unmodified audit opinion and a verified audit trail. **Capacity is built, paid for, and roughly 40% empty**, with capital commitments down to Rs 4.04 crore and CWIP down to Rs 18.0 crore - the build cycle is ending, not starting. [MC] (CALL Jul 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.154) (AR2026 p.139)

**The industry demand base is non-discretionary.** Testing is mandated by regulation; the annual report's own framing is that analytical testing is resilient "underpinned by its non-discretionary role in regulatory compliance and drug safety". [F] (AR2026 p.16)

**The good outcome.** The 200,000 sq ft fills as management describes, the biologics vertical converts three or four sponsors and reaches materiality around FY29, exports hold above 40% as the overseas business-development spend compounds, the Middle East disruption to food trade unwinds, the capex cycle genuinely normalises toward depreciation so fixed-asset turnover crosses 1.0x, and the company deploys its cash into a disciplined acquisition of a regional testing network. sections.title: Research view

blocks.text: At Rs 630 the shares trade above every fair value our model produces. The gap is -92.1% to the bear case, -87.4% to the base case and -83.6% to the bull case, and the full WACC and terminal-growth sensitivity grid spans only Rs 65.7 to Rs 102.6. [F] (NUMBERS) The reverse DCF says the price embeds about 102.4% annual sales growth for five years against a 9.6% base-case equivalent, and the rule-based screen records this as its single red flag. [F] (NUMBERS) **We express no buy, sell or hold view and set no price target.** What we can state is that the arithmetic gap is unusually wide and that a reader should insist on understanding its causes before drawing any conclusion from it.

items: **Roughly a fifth of the gap is a data artefact.** The model's base period is the twelve months to December 2024, with base sales of Rs 329 crore, against FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 407.3 crore. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.115) [E] The model's own Year-1 projection of Rs 358.9 crore has already been exceeded, and its bear-case Year-5 revenue of Rs 406.5 crore is below what the company earned last year. [F] (NUMBERS) A model built on a current base would produce a materially higher fair value.

**A further part is the margin assumption.** The model uses a 29% EBITDA margin against a reported FY26 margin of 35.8% and an ex-other-income margin we estimate at about 34.4%. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.12) [E]

**Part is the discount rate.** A 15% WACC on a company with borrowings at 0.7% of equity, 124x interest cover and a CARE A rating is demanding; the grid shows that alone is worth about 22% of the base value. [F] (NUMBERS) (RATING) (AR2026 p.114) [E]

**Part is the capex rule, and this one works against the price, not for it.** The model reinvests at a 1.82x fixed-asset turnover; CARE measures Vimta's actual fixed-asset turnover at 0.88x. [F] (NUMBERS) (RATING) On the company's actual capital intensity, free cash flow would be lower than modelled, not higher. [AI]

**The residual - and it is the large majority - is a genuine valuation judgement.** The market is paying 8.61x sales, 25.1x EV/EBITDA and 8.16x book for a Rs 416 crore business that generated Rs 147 crore of operating cash flow, spent Rs 100 crore of it on capex, pays a 0.32% dividend yield and has no stated plan for its cash. [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.116) [MC] (CALL May 2026) What justifies that is scarcity, regulatory moat, margin quality, a clean balance sheet and the strategic optionality of a register on which a global TIC major already owns 19.72%. Whether those justify this multiple is the reader's judgement, not ours. [AI]

items: **Horizon.** Nothing in this business resolves quickly. Capacity fills over three to five years on management's own schedule, biologics becomes material in year three, and the electronics vertical cannot scale until new laboratories open in new states. [MC] (CALL May 2026) (CALL Jul 2026) (CALL Feb 2026) Anyone engaging with this name is taking a three-to-five year view or none at all. Equally, the valuation gap identified here is not a three-to-five year problem - it is a today problem, and it does not require patience to observe. [AI]

**Re-review trigger 1 - Q2 FY27 results, due on or before 14 November 2026.** [F] (AR2026 p.73) Test: total income against the Rs 125 crore quarterly run-rate; EBITDA margin against 36%; other income as a share of PBT; whether food sample receipts recovered; whether a second biologics order was disclosed; whether the export share held at 40%.

**Re-review trigger 2 - the FY27 annual report, expected mid-2027.** Test: whether any segment disclosure appears; the bad-debt line; the over-one-year receivable bucket; whether the Rs 14.50 crore "advance for purchase of PPE" unwinds or is explained; FY27 capex against Rs 80 crore or Rs 60 crore; whether directors' remuneration as a share of PAT continues to rise; and the auditor transition at the 37th AGM. [F] (AR2026 p.27)

**Re-review trigger 3 - the next CARE rating action, expected around mid-2027.** [F] (RATING) Test: whether fixed-asset turnover has crossed CARE's 1.0x positive trigger and whether CARE's view of biologics materiality by "FY27-end" was met.

**Re-review trigger 4 - any change in the Eurofins or LCGC holdings, or promoter holding below 35%.** [F] (AR2026 p.138) (NUMBERS) This is the disclosure most likely to change the shape of the investment case in a single filing.

**Re-review trigger 5 - any improvement in disclosure.** If the company begins reporting segment revenue, customer concentration, utilisation or an order book, most of the analytical objections in this report become testable rather than structural, and the entire assessment should be redone. [AI]

blocks.text: **The research view in one paragraph.** Vimta Labs is a well-run, well-financed, honestly accounted contract research and testing business with two genuinely regulator-conferred franchises, a four-year record of margin expansion and export growth, a balance sheet that is essentially unimpeachable, and a management team that reliably delivers operational commitments while reliably missing financial ones. It is also a company that will not tell its owners how concentrated its customers are, what its segments earn, how full its laboratories are, or what work it has in hand - and whose largest single shareholder is a competitor it names on its own earnings calls. Our model says the price sits more than 80% above every fair value it can generate, and while roughly a fifth of that gap is an artefact of a two-year-old revenue base, the great majority is not. No rating and no price target is offered. [AI]
